==English==

===Etymology===
{{bor+|en|la-med|urinātus}}, [[perfect passive participle]] of {{m|la-med|urinō||urinate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), equivalent to {{af|en|urine|-ate|id2=verb}}. Compare {{cog|fr|uriner}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|mīgan}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈjʊəɹɪneɪt/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈjʊɹɪneɪt/|/ˈjʊəɹɪneɪt/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-urinate.ogg|a=US}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|urology}} To pass [[urine]] from the body.
#: {{ux|en|Our new puppy still '''urinates''' on the carpet, but we're housebreaking her.}}
#: {{ux|en|Boys on their campsite should avoid '''urinating''' within 200 feet of the lake.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1877|author=w:John Harvey Kellogg|title=[https://web.archive.org/web/20140811201712/http://etext.virginia.edu/etcbin/ot2www-pubeng?specfile=%2Ftexts%2Fenglish%2Fmodeng%2Fpublicsearch%2Fmodengpub.o2w Plain Facts for Old and Young]
|passage=See that the bladder is emptied just before he goes to bed. Wake him once or twice during the night, and have him '''urinate'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1961|author={{w|Harry E. Wedeck}}|title=Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs|publisher=The Citadel Press|location=New York|page=239|passage=Pliny the Elder, the Roman encyclopedist, declares that to '''urinate''' in a spot where a dog has previously done so results in loss of virility.}}

====Usage notes====
This is a medical term loaned from Latin, but some people prefer to use this word in some social situations as an alternative to {{m|en|piss}} which can be too vulgar and {{m|en|pee}}, {{m|en|wee}}, etc. which can sound embarrassingly childish. The same applies to the noun {{m|en|urine}}.

====Synonyms====
* ''See'' '''[[:Thesaurus:urinate]]'''
